clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 7930 is its operative paragraph, which further exempts William H. Griffin from compulsory retirement for age; the held text reads "for a period of one year ending July 31, 1939". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires that William H. Griffin, who had been exempted for a period of one year ending July 31, 1938 by Executive Order No. 7667 of July 17, 1937, be further exempted for a period of one year; the earlier exemptions are separate instruments that predate this one and cannot end it. The command is a one-person permission for a stated period, so it ended by its own terms on July 31, 1939; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day) under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md, and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No later event is recorded for this clause: no held order text revokes, amends, extends or otherwise cites this order by number or by the person named in it (a search of the held order texts for this order's number finds no citation in any other executive order), and the Federal Register catalog and U.S. Code and eCFR searches report no hit.

research_rationale:
EO 7930 (July 14, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt) is a one-person order exempting William H. Griffin from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, issued under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). This is the stale working-text recheck. The earlier claim quoted an American Presidency Project transcription; the working text is now the machine reading of the Government Printing Office printing held in jobs/mabillon-held-printings (grade machine_read_government_printed_copy, acceptable_as_original false; Executive_Orders_7262-8027.djvu; scanned pages 484-485; closing number tag 7930), and the Photius GPO printing of the same order (HathiTrust hvd.hl272j, jobs/photius-gpo-volumes/output/texts/EO_7930.txt) is also held. Standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. I read the working text in full and compared it word by word with the Photius printing and with the APP transcription: the number, date, title, signatory, authority citation, name of the person and the stated end date agree, and the only differences are OCR noise in the printings (garbled masthead and imprint lines, split or misread letters) that changes no number, date, signatory, name or period. The APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names this order, its date agrees and its text_sha256 equals the held APP file. The Photius page-render check (jobs/photius-gpo-volumes/output/PAGE_CHECKS.csv) passes for this order: tag [No. 7930], dateline 1938-07-14, signatory Franklin D Roosevelt. The order is one recital paragraph and one operative paragraph (the text contains one "I hereby"), so the clause inventory is one whole-order clause. The operative words "for a period of one year ending July 31, 1939" fix the end of the exemption on July 31, 1939; that is the first end, recorded inclusive, with the exclusive reading disclosed. The packet's U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog and held-text name searches report no hit for this order, and a search of the held order texts for its number finds no citation in any other executive order, so no revoking, superseding or extending instrument is recorded.
